record_notes.DCP-LETT-339: Farewell after a merry evening with Herbert; recollection of in-person company, not a written prompt. January 1 is editorially established around the forthcoming Geological Society paper.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-345: Context full reading reconfirms the already accepted Caroline questions answered by 346. Two earlier Darwin letters mentioned remain unspecified; do not duplicate the existing pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-346: Context full reading reconfirms answers to Caroline about Lyell speech, missionary paper and Herschel chronology. Copyist February 29 corrected to Monday February 27. Existing pair retained once.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-347: Declines the Geological Society secretaryship after considering Whewell proposal all day. A proposal is established, but the medium and surviving incoming text are not. Later publication delays cannot enter the contemporary rationale.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-360: Thanks an unlocated Caroline letter about address and globe, then asks his father questions through her. 345 lacks the distinctive address/globe material and is not identified as this prompt. Broad May-June interval retained.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-361: Questions on earthquake waves arise from Cambridge conversation; asks for answers when they meet. Receipt of Whewell signature does not establish an extant covering letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-401: Negotiation of plates follows seeing his publisher. Requests Gould negotiate colouring prices; no incoming letter matched.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-408F: Good Friday gift to Gould and separate Synallaxis note. Gould 409A acknowledges the gift sent that morning; reverse reply only.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-409A: Same-day acknowledgement of Darwin gift strongly answers 408F. Manuscript says dram-bottle while editorial identification is a silver-cased compass; preserve both. Does not prove Darwin later receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-411: Mentions a last Caroline letter expressing difficulty writing; input unlocated. No family letter received for a while and publication forecasts remain forecasts. Same family voice does not identify 345 as the current input.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-431: Congratulations on engagement with a dispatch carried by Josiah. No surviving dispatch text identified; composition on proposal day does not date Darwin receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-476A: Answers a bird-preserver enquiry and thanks Herbert for house searching; actual incoming letter is unlocated. Body combines Geological anniversary yesterday with forthcoming Owen Mastodon lecture, a useful dating lead not yet externally resolved. Raw 1839-1842 interval retained.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-483: Relays Jukes plans after Lonsdale contact; these inputs are unlocated. Explicit thanks for Henslow letter and Mrs Henslow invitation identifies 456 as known by January 4 through a message to Whewell.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-487: Herbert wedding gift is called Forficula. Darwin uniquely describes this note and gift to Emma in 489, proving knowledge by January 20 without a direct response to Herbert.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-496: Requests alteration of Whewell speech heard yesterday evening. Oral address is the antecedent; no incoming letter prompt. Later printed wording does not prove the request was granted.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-504: Whewell sends his translation as a marriage gift to both Darwins. Exact phrase and accompanying note are acknowledged in 506.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-506: Directly thanks Whewell for marriage gift and kind note, identifying 504. Has only dipped into the poem but finished History of Inductive Sciences; preserve different reading states.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-542: Answers unlocated Caroline letter about her eyes, daily life and country tastes. Details match the earlier reference to Caroline in 541 but surviving input is still missing. Lyell Deluge judgement is reported from a visit today.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-571: Asks about Herbert forthcoming event after an uninformative meeting. Marriage in August 1840 is a plausible external upper-bound lead but raw after-June-5 open interval remains held.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-578F: Returns a volume and declines a subscription after an offer to exchange earlier numbers. Offer may be oral or written; no surviving input identified. Raw after-December-1840 interval remains held despite address evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-680A: Explicitly received an unlocated Dieffenbach communication this morning, July 4. Has not read New Zealand book. Translation, plates and questionnaire requests initiate the surviving sequence; no hypothetical input text manufactured.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-682: Reports Colburn permission and price, an unlocated administrative communication, and asks postage and press timing. Delay after family death is event evidence; 680A is an earlier outgoing letter, not its prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-689: Just received an unlocated Dieffenbach letter and sends corrections. Postage question went unanswered; addresses the jack tree and organism queries. Earlier outgoing 682 is not the missing incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-698: Catalogue preserves two quoted Darwin excerpts with editorial paraphrase outside them. Restrict voice to quoted spans. Publication discussion follows unlocated Dieffenbach communication; Hooker praise route is not a surviving direct Hooker letter here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-725: Quoted surviving excerpt discusses reading Dieffenbach chapters and news reports of fighting. Public news and book reading are the evident sources; no direct incoming letter identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-456: Additional full reading: Henslow wedding congratulations end with Mrs Henslow Cambridge invitation, explicitly acknowledged via Whewell in 483.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-489: Additional full reading: Darwin tells Emma that Herbert sent a note and a silver Forficula; unique match to 487. Does not turn Emma response into a reply to Herbert.
